 ORDER 1.

sentences.text: It is the submission of learned counsel for the petitioners that they have been falsely implicated in the case.

As per contents of the FIR, on 17.01.2022, Sub-Instpector, Police Station-Dinara District Shivpuri, received information and searched/raided the premises where three persons were involved in preparation of forged Adhar Cards.

They were taken into custody and from the possession of petitioner No.1 Kaushal Singh 39 Adhar Cards and 3 mobile phones, from petitioner No.2 Satish Tomar, 1 Desi Lodaded Katta, 27 Adhar Cards 70 Sims Cards and photos and addresses of different unknown persons and from Mithun Jha, one laptop, one printer two data cables and one mobile charger were seized.
These persons were selling forged Adhar Cards and Sim Cards to different persons.

4. As submitted by learned counsel for petitioners, present petitioner No.1, Kaushal Singh Bais and petitioner No.2 Satish Tomar were implicated in which name of petitioner No.1 is referred by Satish Tomar, in his memorandum under Section 27 of the Evidence Act.
From the possession of present petitioner No.1, one mobile of Realme Company, one mobile of Vivo Company and one mobile of Mi Company, 39 Adhar Cards were found.
Some of the prosecution witnesses have already been examined and especially seizure witnesses have not supported the story of prosecution.

Alternatively, learned counsel submitted that vide orders dated 12.12.2023, applications preferred by State of Madhya Pradesh under Section 439(2) of Cr.P.C. were allowed and bail of petitioners was recalled vide M.Cr.C. Nos.43144/2023 and M.Cr.C. No.43152/2023 in respect of petitioner No.1 and 2 respectively.
On these grounds, learned counsel for petitioners prayed that petitioners may be given liberty not to surrender and police may inquire from them whenever required.
5. Learned counsel for respondent/State opposed the prayer and submitted that it is the case where hundreds of forged Adhar Cards and Sim Cards have been recovered.
Those Sims cards have been sold to the different persons in Haryana, Delhi and in other States.

Further Investigation is still going on and incidentally one co-accused Pramod destroyed the Adhar Cards and Sim Cards where were found in his possession just to make the case difficult for investigating officer to complete the chain.

Many prosecution witnesses are yet to be examined and this is not a case which can invoke jurisdiction under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.
6.
Heard counsel for the rival parties and perused the documents appended thereto.
7. This is a case where allegations against the petitioners/accused as well as other co-accused are serious in nature.

sentences.text: 2 Cards were sold to different persons and on the basis of those Adhar Cards, Sim Cards were taken by the accused persons from service provider and those Sim Cards were sold to different persons of different States.

Particulars of Adhar Cards/Sim Cards/Articles seized from possession of different accused persons are as under:
Kaushal Singh : 10 Adhar Cards and 3 mobile phones Satish Tomar : 1 Desi Lodaded Katta, 27 Adhar Cards 70 Sims Cards and photos and addresses of different unknown persons.
Mithun Jha : Dell Lap Top, Printer, Data Cable, one Katta and one Black Charger.
Himanshu Sharma: 30 Adhar Cards, 13 Sim Cards, 2 Mobile Phones and Rs.6,000/-.
Vinod : 55 Adhar Cards, 6 Sim Cards and 315  Bore Katta.
8. Independent role of the petitioners/accused may vary but collectively their role appear to be challenging and having wider ramifications in respect of national security and cyber crime.
These Adhar Cards and Sim Cards can be used in NDPS offences, Terrorism related Activities, Cyber Frauds for kidnapping and ransom purposes and for offence of grievous denominations.
9. At present, further investigation in respect of some other co- accused persons is still going on.

Some of the prosecution witnesses have been examined and some of them may have deposed in a different fashion, but that aspect is required to be seen by the trial court holistically after hearing both the parties finally.
This case has its sub-layers to the extent where Anti-National/Anti-Social Activities and its wider ramifications cannot be ruled out.
Under exceptional jurisdiction vested under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C., this is not a fit case for interference.
Trial shall unfold the truth.
10. In the cumulative analysis, petition sans marit is hereby dismissed.
11. A copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance and information.
Certified copy as per rules.
